patterns.summary: Return an HS256-signed JWT for a user id with sub, iss, aud, iat, nbf, exp and a random jti; the secret, issuer, audience, lifetime and clock are parameters.
patterns.title: Create a signed JWT access token (registered claims)
patterns.use_when: Issue a short-lived signed access token for an authenticated user that other services verify with the shared secret, audience and issuer.

patterns.summary: hash_password stores a salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash with its iteration count (at least 600,000); verify_password checks it in constant time; needs_rehash says when to upgrade an old hash.
patterns.title: Hash and verify passwords (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256)
patterns.usage:
stored = hash_password(plain_password)          # at sign-up
if verify_password(attempt, stored):             # at login
    if needs_rehash(stored):
        stored = hash_password(attempt)
patterns.use_when: Store user passwords as salted PBKDF2 hashes at sign-up, check them at login in constant time, and upgrade old hashes after a successful login.

patterns.summary: Parse environment variables described by a caller-supplied schema of (parser, default) pairs; defaults for missing values, ... marks required ones, every problem is reported at once and secret values are never echoed.
patterns.title: Load settings from environment variables with a schema
patterns.use_when: Load an application's settings from environment variables at startup with defaults, type parsing and required values, reporting every invalid value at once.

patterns.summary: Return one 1-based page of a SQLAlchemy 2.0 select as {"items", "total", "page", "page_size", "pages"}, counting over a subquery; page size is capped at 100.
patterns.title: Paginate a SQLAlchemy 2.0 select (page dict)
patterns.usage:
page = paginate(session, select(User).order_by(User.id), page=2, page_size=20)
return {"items": [u.to_dict() for u in page["items"]], "total": page["total"], "pages": page["pages"]}
patterns.use_when: Return one page of a SQLAlchemy 2.0 select together with the total row count and page metadata for a paginated API response.

patterns.summary: GET with requests, retrying connection errors, timeouts, 429 and 5xx with capped exponential backoff, full jitter and numeric Retry-After; session, sleep and randomness are injectable.
patterns.title: GET a URL with retries and exponential backoff (requests)
patterns.use_when: Fetch a URL over HTTP when the server or network can fail transiently: retry connection errors, timeouts, 429 and 5xx with backoff, but fail fast on other 4xx.

patterns.summary: Read users (name, email, optional age) from CSV text or a text stream and return (valid users, errors), each error being {"row", "errors"}; no regex, values never echoed, row count capped.
patterns.title: Parse and validate a users CSV with per-row errors
patterns.use_when: Import users from an uploaded or local CSV (name, email, optional age), keeping valid rows and reporting every problem per row with its line number.

patterns.summary: Refill a per-key token bucket kept in a dict for the elapsed time, take the request's cost if available, and return (allowed, seconds until it would be allowed).
patterns.title: Token-bucket rate limit check with retry-after
patterns.use_when: Decide per client key whether a request is allowed under a rate limit, and how long to wait if not (for a 429 Retry-After), with state in a dict.
